Here's the full picture, including answers to your three asks:

## Where everything stands

**Merged today:** #1134 (OTP backend core — after I cleared the CodeQL false-positive blocking it), **#1140** (shared circuit breaker, closes #1135), **#1143** (SMTP pre-flight, closes #737). Issues #734, #735, #1127, #1135, #737 all verified individually closed.

**Auto-merge armed, landing as CI goes green:**
- **#1148** — the big one: frontend `otp` mode (two-step sign-in, HttpOnly-cookie session, 11-spec fully-local OTP E2E lane in CI) **plus the #1138 nginx `X-Forwarded-Proto` fix**. The 5-agent review came back clean except one docstring overclaim, already fixed. Closes #736 + #1138 on merge.
- **#1144** — test-DB isolation (#1130 + #1133); review found two latent test-integrity gaps (vacuous-lock risk, E2E opt-in narrowed to one env var) — both fixed, E2E now gated on an explicit `DATAQ_E2E=1`.
- **#1145** — OTP purge beat wiring (#1136); review caught a real one (scored 95): no `<=0` guard meant a misconfigured retention value would have instantly deleted **live** sign-in codes. Guard + test added, sibling-sweep pattern.
- **#1142** — the #1137 constant-time floor (1.0s, monotonic-clock remainder, errors deliberately unpadded); reviewed clean, one missing env-table row being added now, then I arm it.

**Still running:** the **#1128** agent (/mcp + PATs in otp-only mode — resumed after the session-limit kill). Queued after the wave: **#1139** (display-name profile completion), the batched `docs/progress.md` update, and **#1141**/**#1147**/**#1146** (filed findings: verify-side timing channel, admin-endpoint mail throttle, mailer CA-bundle option).

## Your two design questions

**Our own mailbox — no for production, yes for local.** Bundling a real outbound mailer in a self-hosted product is a deliverability trap: direct-to-MX from an arbitrary self-hosted IP with no SPF/DKIM/rDNS reputation gets spam-foldered or rejected — precisely on the sign-in critical path — and shipping an open relay inside the appliance is an abuse liability. A vendor-hosted relay would route your users' sign-in metadata through a third party, against the self-hosted posture. Where we *can* remove the setup burden is local/eval: bundle a local inbox (MailHog-style; the #736 E2E lane already built the harder TLS-capable version) so codes land in a web inbox at `localhost:8025` with zero SMTP configuration.

**OTP as the local default — yes for the eval stack, keep bypass for the dev loop.** This is the same lesson as the OpenBao flip: the eval stack's defaults are the security posture evaluators actually run, and bypass-by-default means anyone on the host is admin. Proposal: the published eval compose defaults to `otp` + the bundled inbox, with `setup.sh` prompting your email into the allowlist (fail-closed stays intact — empty allowlist still refuses to boot); contributors' dev loop and the CI bypass lane stay as-is. Both halves are captured in **[#1150](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1150)** — say the word and I'll build it once #1148 is in.

I'll report back as the merge wave and #1128 complete.

- `Fixes #1128` — single issue reference, so the "Closes only closes the first" trap doesn't apply here.

Confirmed no path reaches a validator or a log line with a non-PAT bearer in pat_only mode. `mcp/auth.py` also has zero `log.*` calls, matching `core.auth`'s no-token-content-logging discipline.
2. **Mode ladder agreement with `core.auth`:** `core/auth.py`'s `init_auth()`/`_get_current_user_*` binding order is azure → otp → dev_bypass → fail-closed. `mcp_auth_mode()` is azure_ad → pat_only → dev_bypass → disabled. All three now go through one new `RangeReader`/`read_range` seam: Parquet answers schema *and* `num_rows` from its footer in a couple of small range GETs whatever the object's size, and CSV takes a bounded head read for its schema and a **streamed** pyarrow scan for its count. A run mixing volume with column-freshness still reads the object exactly once. (**2026-07-25 (later still) — #943 shipped, closing the unbounded-flat-file class.** Batch resolution drained every page under the prefix into a list on **every run**, before the runner was even built — so a landing zone with a long history of dated files grew the retained listing without bound on a scheduled path. The listing is now streamed and folded in a single pass keeping only the running bests, so memory is flat regardless of history. The fold reproduces the previous `max()` calls *exactly*, including their first-wins tie-breaking — pinned by a parametrised equivalence test that recomputes the original formulation, because a `>=` would silently flip every tie. **AC 1 as written ('read a bounded number of pages') was not implementable safely and was deliberately not faked:** both stores list ascending, so the newest key — the one `latest` wants — is precisely what a truncated scan misses, and a capped scan would return a confidently wrong older batch. Instead a generous hard limit *refuses* (`BatchListingTooLargeError`, deliberately not a `BatchNotFoundError`, which would skip the run and report success nightly) and a soft limit logs so the cost is visible before it is an incident. The retention test needed two attempts: the first measured *after* the fold returned, where every local is already dead, so it passed against a full materialisation — it now samples peak retention mid-stream. | ✅ | **#737 SMTP pre-flight** — `POST /admin/auth-email/test` (admin-gated, caller's-own-address-only so it structurally can't relay), `_deliver()` stage ladder shared with `send_code`, stage-typed 502s (`connect/tls/auth/send`), redaction proven through the real logging pipeline, Admin-UI "Send test email" button, runbook smoke step. The `/code-review` flow caught a real regression pre-merge: the refactor left the `with smtp` statement unguarded, so a real `smtplib.__exit__` `SMTPResponseException` on QUIT would **replace** the in-flight stage error and escape as a raw 500 on the production sign-in path — the PR's SMTP fakes structurally couldn't see it (never-raising `__exit__`); fixed with an explicit `quit()`-in-`finally` + regression tests. Review also filed [#1147](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1147) (no mailer-appropriate throttle on the endpoint — generic 300/min token class vs the 10/min auth class) | [#1143](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1143) merged 2026-08-02 |
| ✅ | **#1128 `/mcp` in otp-only** — one `mcp_auth_mode()` ladder (`azure_ad → pat_only → dev_bypass → disabled`) mirroring `core.auth`'s exactly (the old gate + log line each re-derived the mode, which is how otp-only ended up unmounted AND mislabeled `dev_bypass`). In `pat_only` the JWT half of `_PatOrJwtVerifier` is genuinely `None` — a non-PAT bearer reaches **no validator** (uniform 401, #849-safe); `dq_sess_` stays rejected by prefix first in every mode; OTP now outranks dev-bypass (a tightening, and it removes a REST-vs-MCP mode disagreement). The OTP-user journey is pinned end-to-end: cookie session mints a PAT via `/me/api-keys` → PAT authenticates all 8 tools on `/mcp`. Each fix half was revert-tested (5/9/4 tests fail respectively); one test was caught passing for the wrong reason (rescued by the suite-wide `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`) and re-pinned | [#1151](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1151) merged 2026-08-02 |
| ✅ | **Findings batch** — every #1134-review finding fixed same-track: **#1135** shared `CircuitBreaker` (one mechanism, per-store state so an OTP brownout can't disable rate limiting; the extraction preserved every #1016 lesson, and the review's one finding — the new monotonic-clock contract vs `rate_limit`'s wall-clock `_now` — was fixed with a dedicated monotonic breaker clock + a discriminating test) → [#1140](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1140); **#1137** constant-time floor on `otp/request` (`AUTH_OTP_REQUEST_MIN_SECONDS`, default 1.0s, monotonic remainder-sleep, errors deliberately unpadded, docs re-scoped to name the SMTP-tail residual; the narrower verify-side channel filed as [#1141](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1141)) → [#1142](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1142); **#1130 + #1133** test-DB isolation (conftest redirects `DATABASE_URL`→`TEST_DATABASE_URL` **before** the engine-building imports — the naive after-import fix was empirically a no-op; lock-test fixtures rebound to the test engine + User-row teardown; review then hardened both its own gaps: visible-row assertions so the lock tests can't go vacuous under URL divergence, and an explicit `DATAQ_E2E=1` opt-in after the redirect silently narrowed the real-infra E2E gate to one env var) → [#1144](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1144); **#1136** `purge_otp_codes` beat crontab (daily 03:37 UTC, staggered; review caught that an unguarded `<=0` retention would instantly delete LIVE codes — service-side no-op guard + test added, sibling-sweep pattern) → [#1145](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1145) |
| ⬜ | Queued next: [#1139](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1139) first-login profile completion (display name — OTP JIT-provisioning leaves it NULL forever) · [#1150](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1150) eval-stack OTP-by-default + bundled local inbox · docs close-out is this PR | — |

The case that actually happens is the FIRST `/me` being throttled, where there is no cached answer to hold and the fix is to stay loading and retry — a different shape from the issue's sketch. **Writing the test is what exposed it**, which is the session's recurring lesson arriving from the other direction: not a test that proves nothing, but a test that refuses to be written because the behaviour isn't there.)
